milestone: HTTP Basic and Digest authentication standardised (static user-ID and password per realm)
quote: The "basic" authentication scheme is based on the model that the client must authenticate itself with a user-ID and a password for each realm.
notes: Static credential; stands in for the API-key era (no dated primary source for API keys found)

milestone: OASIS XACML 1.0: standard policy language with policy decision and enforcement points
quote: This specification defines an XML schema for an extensible access-control policy language.
notes: Quote verified with PDF line numbers stripped

milestone: OAuth 1.0 (RFC 5849): delegated, per-client access without sharing credentials
quote: OAuth provides a method for clients to access server resources on behalf of a resource owner

milestone: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: rate limiting codified (RFC 6585)
quote: The 429 status code indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ("rate limiting").
notes: Fixed per-user limit

milestone: OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749): authorization framework with access tokens
quote: The OAuth 2.0 authorization framework enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service

milestone: OAuth 2.0 access-token scope: grants limited to a stated scope
quote: The authorization and token endpoints allow the client to specify the scope of the access request using the "scope" request parameter.
notes: Same RFC as the row above, different control

milestone: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 final: identity layer on OAuth 2.0
quote: OpenID Connect 1.0 is a simple identity layer on top of the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
notes: Date from the specification reference list ("February 2014"); stored page is errata set 2 (2023)

milestone: Amazon API Gateway launch: managed front door with traffic management and access control
quote: Amazon API Gateway handles all of the tasks involved in accepting and processing up to hundreds of thousands of concurrent API calls, including traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring
notes: Stage is a judgement: central point, static rules

milestone: EU PSD2 Article 97: strong customer authentication required for payment account access (binding on payment providers)
quote: Member States shall ensure that a payment service provider applies strong customer authentication where the payer: (a) accesses its payment account online;
notes: Date is the act date; sector-specific legal requirement

milestone: API Gateway usage plans: per-key throttling and quotas
quote: If you started to use API Gateway after the usage plans feature was rolled out on August 11, 2016, you will automatically have usage plans enabled for you in all supported Regions.
notes: Date from current AWS documentation; InfoQ (api-usageplans-infoq) is secondary corroboration

milestone: Open Policy Agent accepted into the CNCF: general-purpose policy engine
quote: The Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open source, general-purpose policy engine that enables unified, context-aware policy enforcement across the entire stack.
notes: Acceptance date, not first release

milestone: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693): impersonation and delegation tokens
quote: security tokens employing impersonation and delegation
notes: Actor/delegation chains

milestone: Cedar open-sourced: fine-grained authorization policy language and engine
quote: You can use Cedar to express fine-grained permissions as easy-to-understand policies enforced in your applications, and you can decouple access control from your application logic.

milestone: Amazon Verified Permissions generally available (managed Cedar policy store)
quote: Verified Permissions uses Cedar, an open-source language for access control, allowing you to define permissions as easy-to-understand policies.

milestone: Amazon S3 bucket policies (beta): resource-based conditional rules
quote: Bucket policies can restrict access based on AWS account as well as request-based attributes, such as HTTP referrer and IP address.
notes: Stage is a judgement (static account/IP/referrer conditions). Earlier (2006) account-key control not sourced

milestone: AWS IAM preview beta: users and per-user permissions inside an account
quote: IAM enables you to create multiple Users and manage the permissions for each of these Users within your AWS Account.

milestone: AWS IAM generally available with console support
quote: You can now add users to your AWS Account, set groups and permissions for these users, and enable users to call AWS Service APIs

milestone: AWS Organizations generally available with service control policies
quote: Using AWS Organizations, you can create Service Control Policies (SCPs) that centrally control AWS service use across multiple AWS accounts.

milestone: IAM permissions boundaries: ceiling on the permissions delegated admins can grant
quote: Now, you can set a permissions boundary to control the maximum permissions employees can grant to the IAM principals (users and roles) that they create and manage.

milestone: AWS Control Tower generally available with preventive and detective guardrails
quote: they can enable pre-configured guardrails – clearly defined rules for security, operations, and compliance – that prevent deployment of resources that don’t conform to policies
notes: Policy-as-guardrail across accounts

milestone: EU DORA: binding ICT risk-management framework for financial entities (applies from 2025-01-17)
quote: Financial entities shall have in place an internal governance and control framework that ensures an effective and prudent management of ICT risk
notes: Date is the act date; sector-specific; covers cloud use by financial firms

milestone: Packet-filtering gateway (screend, DEC WRL report): table-driven packet screening
quote: One way to restrict access is to prevent certain packets from entering or leaving an organization through its gateways.
notes: Ultrix gateway screen; first sourced packet filter

milestone: HIPAA Security Rule published (effective 2003-04-21): access control and person authentication for health data systems
quote: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights
notes: Sector-specific, not network-specific

milestone: NIST SP 800-94: intrusion detection and prevention systems guidance
quote: An intrusion prevention system (IPS) is software that has all the capabilities of an intrusion detection system and can also attempt to stop possible incidents.
notes: Codification; commercial IPS predates it (unsourced)

milestone: Palo Alto Networks PA-4000: application-aware next-generation firewall
quote: a next-generation firewall that gives organizations unmatched visibility into, and policy control over, applications flowing in and out of their networks

milestone: PCI DSS requirement 6.6 supplement: web application firewalls as a security policy enforcement point
quote: A web application firewall (WAF) is a security policy enforcement point positioned between a web application and the client end point.
notes: Contractual industry standard, not statute

milestone: NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1: guidelines codify stateful inspection beyond packet filtering
quote: Stateful inspection improves on the functions of packet filters by tracking the state of connections and blocking packets that deviate from the expected state.
notes: Codification date; Check Point stateful inspection (c. 1994) not sourced from a primary page

milestone: BeyondCorp (Google): access decided per user and device rather than network perimeter
quote: Virtually every company today uses firewalls to enforce perimeter security. However, this security model is problematic because, when that perimeter is breached, an attacker has relatively easy access to a company’s privileged intranet.
notes: Internal deployment described in paper

milestone: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture
quote: Zero trust (ZT) provides a collection of concepts and ideas designed to minimize uncertainty in enforcing accurate, least privilege per-request access decisions in information systems and services in the face of a network viewed as compromised.

milestone: US Executive Order 14028 directs federal adoption of Zero Trust Architecture
quote: The Federal Government must adopt security best practices; advance toward Zero Trust Architecture
notes: Binding on federal agencies only

milestone: OMB M-22-09 federal zero trust strategy with deadlines to end of FY2024
quote: Federal zero trust architecture (ZTA) strategy, requiring agencies to meet specific cybersecurity standards and objectives by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 2024
notes: Binding on federal agencies only

milestone: EU Machinery Directive 89/392/EEC: essential requirements incl. emergency stop devices
quote: particular attention must be paid to emergency stop devices liable to be subjected to considerable strain
notes: Earlier standards (IEC 60204-1, 1981; EN 418, 1992) not sourced

milestone: OSHA Process Safety Management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) final rule
quote: This section contains requirements for preventing or minimizing the consequences of catastrophic releases of toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive chemicals.
notes: Date from the Federal Register final rule (ind-psmfr)

milestone: IEC 61508-1 first edition: functional safety of programmable safety systems
quote: Sets out a generic approach for all safety lifecycle activities for systems comprised of electrical and/or electronic and/or programmable electronic components
source: Standards Council of Canada catalogue entry for IEC 61508-1:1998
notes: Risk-based safety integrity levels

milestone: IEC 61511-1 first edition: safety instrumented systems for the process industry
quote: gives requirements for the specification, design, installation, operation and maintenance of a safety instrumented system
source: Standards Council of Canada catalogue entry for IEC 61511-1:2003

milestone: EU Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC recast: emergency stop and control-system requirements
quote: located outside the danger zones, except where necessary for certain control devices such as an emergency stop or a teach pendant

milestone: ANSI/ISA-99.01.01-2007: first document of the industrial cybersecurity series (later ISA/IEC 62443)
quote: ANSI/ISA-99.01.01-2007 “Security for Industrial Automation and Control Systems: Concepts, Terminology and Models”. First document of the series.
source: INCIBE, IEC 62443: evolution of the ISA 99
notes: Secondary (Spanish national CERT); ISA primary page not fetched. IEC 62443 dates not sourced

milestone: EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230: protection against corruption of connected machinery
quote: The machinery or related product shall be designed and constructed so that the connection to it of another device, via any feature of the connected device itself
notes: Date is the act date; applies from 2027-01-20 (not verified here)

milestone: US Safe Drinking Water Act: national health-based drinking water standards
quote: The Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) was originally passed by Congress in 1974 to protect public health by regulating the nation’s public drinking water supply.
source: US EPA, Overview of the SDWA
notes: SCADA/telemetry adoption (earlier) has no dated primary source found

milestone: EPA final operator certification guidelines under SDWA section 1419
quote: These guidelines provide States with the minimum standards for the development, implementation and enforcement of operator certification programs for community and nontransient noncommunity public water systems.
notes: Binding through loss of 20 percent of State Revolving Fund grants

milestone: Bioterrorism Act section 401: vulnerability assessments for community water systems, including computer and automated systems
quote: Each community water system serving a population of greater than 3,300 persons shall conduct an assessment of the vulnerability of its system to a terrorist attack or other intentional acts

milestone: NIST SP 800-82: guide to industrial control systems security, naming water and wastewater
quote: ICS are typically used in industries such as electric, water and wastewater, oil and natural gas, transportation

milestone: America's Water Infrastructure Act: risk and resilience assessments incl. electronic and automated systems
quote: Each community water system serving a population of greater than 3,300 persons shall conduct an assessment of the risks to, and resilience of, its system.

milestone: EU NIS2 Directive lists drinking water suppliers and distributors in Annex I
quote: Suppliers and distributors of water intended for human consumption as defined in Article 2, point (1)(a), of Directive (EU) 2020/2184
notes: Date is the act date; transposition due 2024-10-17 (not in stored text)

milestone: EPA withdraws March 2023 memo requiring cybersecurity review in sanitary surveys (reversal)
quote: the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has chosen to rescind the interpretive memorandum issued on March 3, 2023
source: US EPA Office of Water memorandum
notes: Reversal: attempted binding interpretation, withdrawn after litigation; excluded from timing

milestone: EPA enforcement alert on cybersecurity of community drinking water systems
quote: issued an enforcement alert outlining the urgent cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities to community drinking water systems and the steps these systems need to take to comply with the Safe Drinking Water Act
notes: Enforcement of existing section 1433 duties
